html:
SMTO-SKL-0189 — The file didn't match what SMTO expected

GUID: d897d3b9-48e6-5c30-8cf7-045b0f4b8b5b
Slug: github-file-integrity-failed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • Either the file you asked to upload has changed or been damaged since SMTO saved it, or a download from GitHub arrived incomplete. SMTO stopped so it wouldn't send or keep a broken file.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were uploading, attach a fresh copy of the file using Add context › Add files to conversation, then ask the Agent to upload that new copy. The saved copy no longer matches what was recorded, so a new copy is needed.
  2. If you were downloading, ask the Agent to download the file again. Downloads only read from GitHub, and SMTO didn't keep the incomplete copy, so trying again is safe.
  3. If the download keeps failing, check your internet connection and whether github.com is working. An unstable connection can cut a download short every time.

What success looks like

  • The upload appears on GitHub, or the downloaded file appears in the Conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit the saved file and upload it under the same name; attach a new copy instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A GitHub file transfer failed its integrity check: the upload source's bytes differ from the artifact's recorded size or SHA-256, or a download without Content-Encoding received a byte count different from its Content-Length.

What this means

  • Source bytes differ from registered size/SHA-256, or an unencoded download length differs from its numeric Content-Length. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Source bytes differ from registered size/SHA-256, or an unencoded download length differs from its numeric Content-Length.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact artifact revision/hash and whether download encoding affects the length check.

How to fix it

  • For uploads, inspect or recreate the source artifact; its stored bytes no longer match the recorded size/SHA-256, so register a new artifact rather than reusing the existing identity with modified bytes. For downloads, the received length differed from Content-Length; repeat the read-only download once GitHub responds normally.
  • Inspect or recreate the source artifact; the recorded size/hash or download length did not match. Do not upload modified bytes under an existing artifact identity.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended complete bytes pass applicable integrity checks before use.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
